messages.author: 456d80b69823f2d0
messages.subject: multiple plots per page
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am a new user of ggplot2, so I am definetly in the learning stage.
I am wanting to put multiple plots in one window. When I have tried
to use par(mfrow=c(2,2)) in conjunction with qplot, it doesn't work.
I have had to put all of my plots in a list and print them using a for
loop, but this seems ridculously complicated as compared to
par(mfrow=c()). Is there a better way?

plots <- list()

plots[[length(plots)+1]] <- qplot(mu[,
3],geom="density",main="1993",xlab=expression(paste(mu)))
plots[[length(plots)+1]] <- qplot(mu[,
4],geom="density",main="1994",xlab=expression(paste(mu)))
plots[[length(plots)+1]] <- qplot(mu[,
5],geom="density",main="1995",xlab=expression(paste(mu)))
plots[[length(plots)+1]] <- qplot(mu[,
6],geom="density",main="1996",xlab=expression(paste(mu)))

numPlots = length(plots)
plotCols = 2
plotRows = 2
pdf("mu.post93-96.pdf", width=4*plotCols, height=4*plotRows)

grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(plotRows, plotCols)))
vplayout <- function(x, y)viewport(layout.pos.row = x, layout.pos.col
= y)

for (i in 1:numPlots)
{
curRow = ceiling(i/plotCols)
curCol = (i-1) %% plotCols + 1
print(plots[[i]], vp = vplayout(curRow, curCol ))
}

dev.off()

Hi Bonnie,
The usual way to do this in ggplot is to melt() the data and use
faceting. If you provide a reprodicible example I will be happy to
show you how that can be done.

Best,
Ista
